en: A woodpecker's sharp, pointed beak acts as a wedge to split tree bark and find insects.
The slippery mucus covering a mudfish reduces water friction, helping it escape from predators.
The gravitational pull of the moon causes the regular high and low tides in Manila Bay.
Black sand beaches in Cagayan contain magnetite, a naturally occurring mineral that is attracted to magnets.
A lightning strike during a thunderstorm is a massive, visible discharge of static electricity in the sky.
Fireflies in the mangroves of Palawan produce their own glowing light through a chemical reaction in their bodies.
Insect-eating bats in Philippine caves use echolocation, bouncing sound waves off objects to navigate in the dark.
The natural hot springs in Los Baños, Laguna, are heated by geothermal energy from deep underground.
The fast-flowing water of Maria Cristina Falls possesses kinetic energy that spins turbines to generate electricity.
Dried coconut meat, called copra, stores chemical energy that is released as heat when burned for fuel.
The strong jaw muscles of a saltwater crocodile act as levers to generate immense biting force.
The broad leaves of a banana plant catch air resistance, which can easily uproot the tree during strong typhoons.
